args.title: Flag placement on hidden cells
args.description: Flags may be placed only on hidden cells.
args.given_when_then: Given an in-progress game and a hidden cell When the player flags it Then the cell state becomes flagged and flag_count increases by one; Given a revealed cell When the player flags it Then the board is unchanged.

@dataclass
class Game:
    """Game.

    cells: the Cell records this Game owns, one dict each with the keys id (str), row (int), column (int), has_mine (bool), adjacent_mine_count (int), state (str).
    """
    id: str
    difficulty: str = "Beginner"
    status: str = "ready"
    started_at: Optional[str] = None
    ended_at: Optional[str] = None
    elapsed_seconds: int = 0
    mine_count: int = 10
    flag_count: int = 0
    cells: List[Dict[str, Any]] = field(default_factory=list)
    events: List[Any] = field(default_factory=list)

    def to_dict(self) -> Dict[str, Any]:
        return {
            k: v for k, v in self.__dict__.items() if not k.startswith("_")
        }

kwargs.interface_contract:
- Action `start_game`: params [`difficulty`] — Discards any current board and timer and sets up a new board for the chosen difficulty (Beginner, Intermediate or Expert) with rows, columns and mine_count taken from that difficulty, status ready, elapsed_seconds 0, flag_count 0, no started_at or ended_at, and no mine layout fixed yet; allowed in any status.
- Action `reveal_cell`: params [`row`, `column`] — On the first reveal of a ready game, places mines avoiding the target cell and its neighbours, sets started_at, and moves the game to in_progress; then reveals the hidden, unflagged target cell, expanding zero-count regions, and may end the game as lost (on a mine) or won (when all safe cells are revealed); ignored if the game is won or lost, the position is outside the board, or the cell is already revealed or flagged.
- Action `toggle_flag`: params [`row`, `column`] — Cycles a hidden cell to flagged (flag_count increases by one) or a flagged cell back to hidden (flag_count decreases by one), without starting the timer; allowed only while the game is ready or in_progress, and ignored for revealed cells or positions outside the board.
- A newly created `Game` (constructed with only its required fields) holds: id set to the given identifier; difficulty "Beginner"; status "ready"; started_at null; ended_at null; elapsed_seconds 0; mine_count 10; flag_count 0; cells is an empty list until the first reveal lays out the board; events empty.
- Field `status` holds exactly one of: "ready" (New game, no cell revealed yet, timer not started, mine layout not fixed.); "in_progress" (First reveal has happened and the session has not ended.); "won" (Every non-mine cell has been revealed; terminal.); "lost" (A mine was revealed; terminal.)
- Field `difficulty` holds exactly one of: "Beginner" (9 rows by 9 columns with 10 mines.); "Intermediate" (16 rows by 16 columns with 40 mines.); "Expert" (16 rows by 30 columns with 99 mines.)
- Field `cells[].state` holds exactly one of: "hidden" (Cell not yet revealed and not flagged; default state.); "revealed" (Cell has been opened; shows a mine or an adjacency count.); "flagged" (Player marked the hidden cell as a suspected mine.)
- A refusal raises `InvalidActionError` when An action is attempted that the rules do not allow, such as flagging or revealing after the game has been won or lost, revealing a flagged or revealed cell, or a position outside the board; the board and session are left unchanged.
kwargs.other_rules:
- Adjacency count: Given a game with mines placed and a safe cell at a position When the mine layout is fixed Then the cell's adjacent_mine_count equals the number of mines in its up to eight neighbouring cells.
- Zero expansion: Given a hidden cell with adjacent_mine_count 0 in an in-progress game When the player reveals it Then all its neighbouring hidden cells are revealed and any neighbour with count 0 continues the expansion recursively.
- Zero expansion stops at numbered cells: Given a zero-count reveal that reaches a neighbour with count greater than 0 or a flagged neighbour When expansion runs Then that neighbour is revealed only if hidden and not flagged, and expansion does not continue beyond it.
- First-click safety: Given a game in ready status When the first cell is revealed Then mines are placed so that the revealed cell and all its neighbours have has_mine false, and the layout is fixed.
- Flag removal: Given a flagged cell in an in-progress game When the player removes the flag Then the cell returns to hidden and flag_count decreases by one; Given a flagged cell When the player attempts to reveal it Then the cell remains flagged and is not revealed.
- Right-click cycle: Given a hidden cell When the player right-clicks it Then it becomes flagged; Given a flagged cell When the player right-clicks it Then it becomes hidden; Given a revealed cell When right-clicked Then it is unchanged.
- Mine counter may go negative: Given a game with mine_count M and flag_count F When the counter is displayed Then it shows M minus F, including negative values when F exceeds M.
- Loss on mine reveal: Given an in-progress game When the player reveals a mine Then status becomes lost, ended_at is set, all mine cells are shown as revealed, and flagged cells without mines are marked as wrong.
- Win on all safe cells revealed: Given an in-progress game When the last non-mine cell is revealed Then status becomes won, ended_at is set, and every unrevealed mine cell becomes flagged.
- Terminal state rejects changes: Given a game in won or lost status When the player reveals or flags any cell Then the board and status are unchanged; When the player restarts Then a new game is created.
- Timer starts on first reveal: Given a game in ready status When the first cell is revealed Then started_at is set and elapsed time begins; Given a game in ready status When a flag is placed Then the timer does not start.
- Timer stops at session end: Given an in-progress game When the session is won or lost Then elapsed_seconds is fixed at the value at that moment and no longer increases.
- Timer display cap: Given elapsed time greater than 999 seconds When the timer is displayed Then it shows 999.
- Invalid operations ignored: Given any game state When the player reveals a revealed cell, acts after game end, or targets a position outside the board Then the board and session state are unchanged.
- Restart resets session: Given a game in any status When the player starts a new game at a chosen difficulty Then a new board is created with status ready, elapsed time zero, and no mine layout fixed.
- Board edge boundaries: Given a cell on the board edge or corner When adjacency is computed Then only neighbours inside the board are counted, giving fewer than eight neighbours.

import copy

from src.domain.game import Game


def make_in_progress_game(target_state: str) -> Game:
    """Build an in-progress 9x9 Beginner board with a full 81-cell grid.

    Every cell is safe with adjacent_mine_count 0, so no rule about mines,
    expansion, or winning is in play. Only the state of cell (4, 4) differs
    between the two scenarios.
    """
    game = Game(id="game-flag-1")
    game.difficulty = "Beginner"
    game.status = "in_progress"
    game.started_at = "2024-01-01T10:00:00"
    game.elapsed_seconds = 0
    game.mine_count = 10
    game.flag_count = 0
    game.cells = [
        {
            "id": f"r{row}c{col}",
            "row": row,
            "column": col,
            "has_mine": False,
            "adjacent_mine_count": 0,
            "state": "hidden",
        }
        for row in range(9)
        for col in range(9)
    ]
    for cell in game.cells:
        if cell["row"] == 4 and cell["column"] == 4:
            cell["state"] = target_state
    return game


def find_cell(game: Game, row: int, column: int) -> dict:
    for cell in game.cells:
        if cell["row"] == row and cell["column"] == column:
            return cell
    raise AssertionError(f"no cell at ({row}, {column})")


def test_flagging_a_hidden_cell_sets_state_to_flagged_and_increments_flag_count():
    # Given an in-progress 9x9 board, all cells safe with count 0,
    # and cell (4, 4) is hidden. flag_count starts at 0.
    game = make_in_progress_game(target_state="hidden")

    # When the player flags cell (4, 4).
    game.toggle_flag(row=4, column=4)

    # Then the cell is hidden -> flagged: its state is "flagged".
    assert find_cell(game, 4, 4)["state"] == "flagged"
    # And flag_count goes from 0 to 1 (one flag placed).
    assert game.flag_count == 1


def test_flagging_a_revealed_cell_leaves_the_board_unchanged():
    # Given the same in-progress 9x9 board, but cell (4, 4) is revealed.
    # The cell is not hidden, so a flag may not be placed on it.
    game = make_in_progress_game(target_state="revealed")
    board_before = copy.deepcopy(game.cells)
    flags_before = game.flag_count

    # When the player tries to flag cell (4, 4).
    # The rule ignores flagging of revealed cells, so no exception is expected.
    game.toggle_flag(row=4, column=4)

    # Then every cell is exactly as it was, including cell (4, 4) still revealed.
    assert game.cells == board_before
    assert find_cell(game, 4, 4)["state"] == "revealed"
    # And flag_count is unchanged at 0.
    assert game.flag_count == flags_before
